title.narrative: BOS program för ungdomar och media CS för EU
BOS programme for youth and media CS for EU - Youth media EU

description.narrative:
The MAY4DD Programme focused on linking youth participation with media development. By fostering partnerships between youth organisations and independent local media, it aimed to strengthen democratic dialogue and amplify youth voices.
Many young people in Serbia are politically invisible, marginalised, and only symbolically included in decision-making. The Programme addressed this by empowering youth to become active participantsco-creating campaigns, producing media content, engaging with local authorities, and influencing decisions. This shift is illustrated by concrete examples: in Vranje, youth advocacy led to government action toward establishing a youth centre; in Ni, young people presented policy recommendations directly to the Mayors Office; and in Prijepolje, youth-driven media campaigns promoted informed dialogue and engagement with credible information. Overall, these cases demonstrate a transition from passive inclusion to meaningful youth participation in community and policy processes.
Many local media outlets in Serbia face financial constraints and relie on reactive, event-driven reporting, with youth issues often underrepresented or framed through crisis narratives. Through MAY4DD support, local media were empowered to diversify topics relevant to young peoplesuch as digital privacy, activism, gender equality, and mental healthwhile adopting investigative formats, engaging youth as contributors, and expanding into multimedia storytelling.Examples illustrate this shift: the Zoomer documentary sparked public debate and repositioned media as a platform for dialogue; Boom93 in Poarevac enabled youth to produce content on disinformation, strengthening community engagement with verified information; and MentalHUBs reporting manual encouraged more ethical and responsible coverage of mental health. Overall, local media evolved from reactive reporting toward a more inclusive, investigative, and socially responsible role.
Several initiatives supported by the Programme helped strengthen local dialogue between civil society and public institutions. Key shifts included greater participation of public officials in youth-led debates, budget reallocations toward youth initiatives, increased recognition of civil society organisations as relevant partners, and the uptake of project-based recommendations. Examples illustrate this progress: in Subotica, intercultural dialogue projects fostered cooperation among diverse youth groups and encouraged more consistent engagement from local authorities; meanwhile, the Young Farmers of Serbia platform improved transparency and access to agricultural subsidies, building trust between rural youth and institutions. Overall, institutional actors moved from cautious involvement to more regular participation, signalling a gradual normalisation of dialogue between civil society and government.
Through the development of educational tools such as manuals, gamified quizzes, and youth-friendly video formats, teachers independently adopted and disseminated materials resulted in youth audiences engaged critically with digital topics such as AI, algorithmic bubbles, and doomscrolling. Also some schools beyond initial target areas requested workshops. For example in Branievo district and beyond, some 84 teachers voluntarily integrated media literacy materials into classroom activities despite the absence of formal curricula requirements. With this the Programme helped fill an institutional gap in media literacy education and encouraged bottom-up diffusion of democratic skills.

Organisationen Belgrade Open School (BOS), Serbien har hos Sida ansökt om 20 miljoner kronor för finansiering av programmet "CS4EU-Civil Society as a Force for a Change in the Serbia's EU Accession Process" under perioden 2021-2024.
BOS är officiellt registrerad i Serbien som en civilsamhällesorganisation (”Association of citizens”) sedan 1996. BOS förekommer inte på någon av EU:s sanktionslistor och har erhållit stöd från Sida sedan 2012 och varit en direkt avtalspart sedan 2016.
Insatsens totala budget är 20 miljoner kronor och Sida är enda bidragsgivaren. Ungefär 10 miljoner kronor är planerat vidareförmedlas till lokala civilsamhällesorganisationer som arbetar med framför allt unga och media.
Insatsen syftar till att ge det civila samhällets organisationer bättre möjlighet att ta aktiv del i Serbiens EU närmande process. Belgrad Open School ska genom detta program stödja kapacitetsuppbyggnad och stärka synergier mellan media, ungdomsorganisationer och ungdomar som arbetar med att ytterligare demokratisera det serbiska samhället. Programmets huvudsyfte är att uppmuntra unga människor att engagera sig i frågor som rör media och delta aktivt i det civila samhället genom att främja faktabaserad och oberoende journalistik.
Det är Sidas bedömning att det föreslagna programmet är i linje med Sveriges Resultatstrategi för reformsamarbete med Östeuropa, Västra Balkan och Turkiet för perioden 2014-2021 (förlängd) och att insatsen kommer bidra till ökad kapacitet hos serbiska civilsamhällesorganisationers att påverka och skapa bättre möjligheter för demokratisk samhällsutveckling och Serbiens EU-närmande, inklusive dess värdegrund.

The contribution aims to activate young people in relation to development and reform agenda, which in turn contributes towards the achievement of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs). Activating the youth happens in stages: Awareness, Understanding and Action. Media plays important role to advance SDGs as powerful driver for advocacy, action and accountability.
The programme aims to encourage active citizenship: to identify and promote young change-makers, and to support free media as an actor of change working for democratic values and human rights.
